joint_invariant.name: JOINT_BINARY_BLOCK_GRAPH
joint_invariant.definition: Graph on sibling variables with an edge {u,v} whenever u,v occur together in a binary clause of either sibling A or B.
joint_invariant.base_block: For R44AS siblings, A contributes edges 3-4 and 1-4; B contributes 5-6 and 3-6. Their union is the connected path 1-4-3-6-5.
joint_invariant.connector_effect: R44BZ connector clauses all have width 3, so they contribute no joint-binary edges.
joint_invariant.consequence: Connected components of the raw joint-binary graph are exactly the five-variable R44AS blocks. The hidden block partition is recovered in polynomial time.

local_transport_theorem.discovery: Enumerate the constant candidate space independently in each recovered block and retain only exact clause-subsumption transports.

synchronization_theorem.edge_gadget: The 12-clause pi-orbit connector between adjacent recovered blocks.
synchronization_theorem.finite_relation: Among the 2 x 2 pairs of locally valid B->A transports, exactly one pair preserves the connector clause set under the transport check: (pi,pi), where pi={1:-3,3:-5,4:6,5:-1,6:-4} in local coordinates.
synchronization_theorem.global_effect: Because the recovered block graph is connected, edge consistency propagates pi to every block. No bounded-support enumeration is required.

complexity.block_recovery: O(S) to polynomial in encoded sibling size using binary-clause hashing/graph components
complexity.local_domains: 3840 candidates per five-variable block, hence O(number_of_blocks * poly(S)) with constant factor
complexity.edge_checks: constant 2x2 local-domain relation per block edge after local filtering; polynomial overall
complexity.end_to_end: polynomial in the raw R44BZ sibling encoding

rank_and_replay.model_lift: The discovered global signed transport directly maps a deleted-sibling model into a retained-sibling model; retained model lifts to parent by setting the shared pivot to the retained branch value.

next_exact_question: Construct a growing maxdef-critical both-nonterminal family in which individual siblings are congruence-rigid and the JOINT binary block graph no longer exposes a constant-size block decomposition with a uniquely synchronizing transport domain, or prove a broader polynomial joint-structure recovery theorem.
